name: Green Racquet-tail
rangeDescription: Northern philippines (lowlands of luzon and marinduque)
description: A rare medium-sized parrot of lowland and foothill forest on Luzon. The two central tail feathers have extended shafts ending in a racket shape.

name: Violet-capped Woodnymph
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Common hummingbird of both montane and lowland forests and woodlands. Also visits feeders and gardens.

name: Sulphury Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela, trinidad, and the guianas to northern bolivia and amazonian brazil
description: Medium-sized flycatcher with a plumage pattern—brownish above, yellow below—that recalls Tropical Kingbird, but Sulphury Flycatcher is much darker gray on the face and head and has a contrasting white throat. Inhabits a variety of forest types but is most common in flooded and edge habitats with many palms—especially common in Moriche palm stands in savanna regions.

name: Black-headed Berryeater
rangeDescription: Coastal southeastern brazil (alagoas and eastern bahia to northeastern paraná)
description: Big and chunky cotinga that is usually spotted perching motionless in the canopy of humid forests. The black head contrasts with a red iris.

name: Burchell's Starling
rangeDescription: Southern angola to western zambia, namibia, mozambique, and northern south africa
description: A large, long-tailed, iridescent blue-green to purple glossy starling with barred wings, and a round-tipped tail. Pairs, groups, and small flocks are resident in dry savanna, especially near thorn trees, where they have become common in camps and often associate with humans.

name: Black-chinned Mountain Tanager
rangeDescription: Humid andes of western colombia and western ecuador
description: Large and colorful tanager of Andean cloud forest in western Ecuador and western Colombia. Plumage is golden-yellow with a black head, blue wing patch, and yellow stripe on rear crown.

name: Sharp-tailed Tyrant
rangeDescription: Eastern bolivia to south-central brazil, eastern paraguay, and northeastern argentina
description: A handsome tiny flycatcher with a long spiky tail. Note the conspicuous broad white eyebrow and white chin.

name: Salmon-crested Cockatoo
rangeDescription: Southern moluccas (seram, ambon, saparua, and haruku)
description: A large white cockatoo with a pinkish cast to many feathers and yellow under the wings. The bright salmon color may be mostly concealed unless the crest is raised.

name: Crested Hornero
rangeDescription: Chaco of southeastern bolivia to western paraguay and northern argentina
description: A mostly terrestrial and chunky light brown bird of the north and central Chaco, from central Argentina to Western Paraguay and extreme SE Bolivia. Distinguished from Rufous Hornero by crest, from Lark-like Brushrunner by plain plumage, and from Cachalotes by dull plumage, smaller bill and size, and dark iris.

name: Loja Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern ecuador and far northern peru
description: Small, mouse-like bird found in the high Andes of southern Ecuador and northern Peru. Male is mostly dark gray; female has brown upperparts and gray underparts.

name: Alström's Warbler
rangeDescription: Western and southern china; winters to thailand, cambodia, and northern vietnam
description: Sprightly, small warbler that poses a bevy of identification issues. Dull olive above and yellow below, with a bright eyering and a gray crown bound in by black stripes.

name: Ring-billed Gull
rangeDescription: North america; winters to southern mexico, bahamas, and greater antilles
description: Fairly small gull, common and widespread throughout most of North America. Breeding adults are white-headed with a bold black ring around the bill; nonbreeding adults have smudgy brown markings on the head.

name: Bartlett's Tinamou
rangeDescription: Tropical western amazonian brazil, eastern peru, and northern bolivia
description: Small tinamou of floodplain rainforest. Reddish brown with limited black barring on the wings.

name: Eurasian Wigeon
rangeDescription: Breeds northern and central eurasia; winters to northern africa and southern asia
description: Breeding males are beautiful and distinctive with rich reddish-brown head, buffy forehead, pearly gray body, and pinkish breast. Look for large white wing patches in flight.

name: Angola Helmetshrike
rangeDescription: Western angola (gabela escarpment)
description: A gregarious, cartoonish, mostly gray-brown helmetshrike with a black head, piercing orange eyes, red legs and eye-wattles, and an orange-tipped red bill. Pairs and flocks of 4–10 inhabit mature dry and secondary forest, plantations, and thickets in a narrow range along the Angolan escarpment, where it is endemic and endangered.

name: Red-chested Buttonquail
rangeDescription: Savanna and scrub of northern and eastern australia
description: Small, dark, secretive buttonquail with pale eye, found in dense grassland habitats, where most commonly observed exploding from cover and flying rapidly away. In flight, note the fairly uniformly dark upperparts, with less contrast between flight feathers and coverts than in most other buttonquail.

name: Bare-headed Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Highlands of northeastern borneo
description: Thickset, dark-gray-brown laughingthrush with a bright-candy-red bill, broad blue moustache patches, and a sickly-looking bare yellow crown. Endemic to the highlands of north-central Borneo.

name: Blackish Nightjar
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to southern venezuela, the guianas, bolivia, and brazil
description: A fairly small, dark nightjar found in the lowlands and foothills of northern South America. Intricately patterned with dark browns and grays; lacks any obvious features like a collar (although it sometimes shows a small white patch on the side of the neck).

name: Syrian Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Southeastern europe, transcaucasia, türkiye and iran to israel and jordan
description: Very similar to Great Spotted Woodpecker, differing mainly by the incomplete cheek band and the lack of black at the base of the bill. Males have a red nape, black in females.

name: Bridled Sparrow
rangeDescription: Arid central plateau of mexico (puebla to oaxaca)
description: Very handsome but rather local sparrow endemic to interior southern Mexico. Found in scrubby oak woodland and brushy cactus scrub of dry tropical foothills and interior valleys.
